A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALPS research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ALPS evaluations on Maze2D–PointMass and OGBench locomotion tasks, component ablations, and cluster-count experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds visual-antmaze, manipulation, and eigenvector-count results. The separately attributed baseline results in Appendix B.3 do not negate these original contributions.

M1.justification: The ALLO representation, eigenvalue scaling, k-means cluster graph, Dijkstra planning, dynamics objective, behavior prior, and CEM procedure remain unchanged. Expanded rollout explanations clarify existing operations. Convolutional processing for image observations was already documented in v1 Appendix E.2.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained Maze2D image observations and state-based locomotion tasks, v2 evaluates visual-antmaze using RGB observations and adds cube-single, cube-double, and scene manipulation. These introduce substantially different observation conditions and object-manipulation requirements.

E2.justification: New Appendix B.3 and Table 4 compare ALPS with HILP, SAW, RLDP, and TD-JEPA across selected OGBench tasks. Their scores are explicitly imported from their papers, rather than newly reproduced. PcLast and the six original main-table comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the generic 1M-step, batch-1024 training specification with separate pixel settings of 500K steps and batch 256, and adds pixel evaluation checkpoints at 300K/400K/500K. Manipulation uses eight clusters and sampling discount 0.2. The existing state-based checkpoint and rollout protocol remains; these reported changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G.3 and Table 10 add a controlled eigenvector-count ablation using D = 2, 8, 16, 24, 32, and 48 on four antmaze datasets while fixing cluster counts. The component ablations, cluster-count analysis, PcLast reproduction investigation, and teleport case study already existed in v1.

E5.justification: v2 specifies four seeds for the added pixel-based OGBench tasks while retaining eight for state-based tasks and ten for the PcLast comparison. The declared significance threshold changes from 0.01 to 0.001. Mean/standard-deviation reporting, Figure 3 standard errors, and the Holm-corrected Wilcoxon procedure remain.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive visual, manipulation, additional-baseline, and eigenvector-ablation results and revises many retained scores. For example, reported ALPS humanoidmaze-giant-stitch success changes from 38 ± 8 to 62 ± 6; new cube-double success is 2 ± 1. However, v2 reports humanoidmaze-large-stitch as 39 ± 6 in Tables 2/13 but 56 ± 5 in Tables 3/17, leaving that revised result inconsistent.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 recasts the existing CTD derivation as a theorem with explicit connected-undirected graph assumptions and adds a truncation-error bound and discounted-transition-operator formula. Section 4 also introduces a dual-variable scaling equality whose minus sign is incorrectly outside the square root, inconsistent with the retained eigenvalue relationship.

C1.justification: The central claims about Laplacian representations, hierarchical planning, and outperforming common OGBench baselines remain. The conclusion changes the claimed condition favoring hierarchy from imperfect example trajectories in v1 to limited state-action coverage in v2; these are substantively different conditions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantial applicability limitation: it attributes multi-object manipulation failures to global representations entangling independently varying objects and proposes factorization. It also discusses large-graph CTD degeneration, interprets eigenvector sensitivity, and proposes asymmetric representations and hitting times. The teleport limitation itself was already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 supplies code and project-page links, dataset-generation noise magnitudes, manipulation-specific settings, and more explicit baseline checkpoint information. Most architecture and optimizer details were already documented. It removes v1's explicit statement that ALLO transition pairs are sampled within the same episode, without establishing a procedural change.

R1.justification: Section 7 and Appendix B broaden discussion of contrastive subgoal representations and recent alternatives, including SAW, RLDP, and TD-JEPA. v2 removes the claim that HILP's smoothness obscures partition boundaries and adds CTD-degeneration and hierarchical-RL references. The central positioning relative to PcLast and Laplacian representation learning remains.

P1.justification: The main eight-section narrative remains intact. v2 revises background and planning explanations, expands baseline descriptions, moves statistical testing into Appendix C, and reorganizes appendix headings. Affiliation, publication-header, and acknowledgement text also changes.

P2.justification: The main results table expands substantially, and v2 adds baseline-comparison, eigenvector-ablation, and manipulation/visual per-task tables. New Figures 5 and 7 illustrate dataset trajectories and manipulation environments. Figure 1 changes from medium to large pointmaze, and Figure 4 reorders panels; the cluster-count and teleport visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the broader evaluations expose an important multi-object failure boundary, while additional comparators and the eigenvector ablation improve assessment of ALPS's applicability and design choices. Code-access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are tempered by the new conflicting humanoidmaze-large-stitch scores in Tables 2/13 versus 3/17 and the incorrect scaling equality in Section 4, limiting the overall quality improvement.
